elements_not_encoded.text: Manage urgently:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Header of the urgent management list.

elements_not_encoded.text: If patient just had a seizure 20.
If aggressive/disruptive 35.
If recent head injury 30.
If suicidal thoughts or plans 34.
If difficulty breathing, respiratory rate > 30, oxygen saturation < 94% or oxygen saturation machine not available, give face mask oxygen.
Check glucose: if < 3 (or < 4 if diabetes) or ≥ 11.1 19.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Glucose is a routine vital; abnormal values route to page 19.

elements_not_encoded.text: If thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, sunken eyes, decreased urine, give oral rehydration solution. If unable to drink or BP < 90/60, give sodium chloride 0.9
Consider involuntary admission if signs of mental illness and refuses treatment/admission and a danger to self, others, own reputation or financial interest/pro
If HIV positive with recent positive cryptococcal antigen test, refer for urgent lumbar puncture (LP).
Look for delirium, mania, psychosis, intoxication, withdrawal or poisoning and manage before referral:
elements_not_encoded.reason: Introduces the diagnosis boxes; each box is encoded as its own diagnosis rule.

elements_not_encoded.text: If no other sedation given, give diazepam 10mg orally.
Give thiamine 200mg IM.
If pulse irregular, chest pain or BP ≥ 140/90, do ECG and discuss with specialist or local poison helpline 200.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ECG and discussion with specialist/poison helpline.

elements_not_encoded.text: If alcohol withdrawal, also give thiamine 200mg IM and oral rehydration solution.
Give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L 6 hourly.
If ≥ 8 hours since last alcohol, refer for alcohol detoxification programme.
Check for head injury.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Instruction to check for head injury (routes to head injury care); not a diagnostic criterion.

elements_not_encoded.text: Refer urgently unless:
Patient with known schizophrenia who is otherwise well, give routine schizophrenia care 162.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral exception: known schizophrenia, routine care.

elements_not_encoded.text: Patient with diabetes and low glucose on insulin. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves with dextrose, no need to refer, give routine diabetes care 145.
Patient with known alcohol use who is otherwise well. If abnormal thoughts/behaviour resolves once sober, no need to refer 165.
